subject: Action needed: Brightlane POC — long-prompt stream drops & SDK behavior
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evan Barnes <evan@brightlane.io>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Action needed: Brightlane POC — long-prompt stream drops & SDK behavior

Hi team,

Brightlane hit a blocking issue during yesterday's POC run. When they send long context+instructions (~12k tokens) the streaming response intermittently cuts out after ~30–60s and the SDK client ends with a connection reset without a clear error. They reproduced this across two regions (us-west-2 / us-east-1) and see it more often in our dedicated demo pool. Evan attached a sample payload and a short session dump.

Impact: Brightlane is demoing this to two prospects next week; they expect us to provide a mitigation and an ETA.

What we have so far (from field notes):
- Observed behavior: streaming SSE stops mid-response; SDK returns a socket close and no partial final token. No immediate 5xx from runtime.
- Example trace id: bf3a-9c21-5532 (attached session_dump_20260915.txt)
- Temporary workaround that helped in one run: split prompt into 6k token chunks and synthesize client-side; not ideal.

As Sales Eng I need two things:
1) Short-term: a clear mitigation we can give Brightlane (config or SDK workaround) so they can continue demos.
2) Product ask: a per-route streaming "grace window" toggle or a client-visible retry that preserves streaming partials, plus a plan to prevent regressions for long-context streaming.

Karthik / Dev — can you triage the BF trace and advise on root cause and a short-term mitigation? Also advise if we should open an exemption for Brightlane's dedicated pool (latency/queue settings). Evan, can you confirm whether the SDK client is the official Redwood JS SDK or a fork?

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Email: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 415 555 1234

Attachments: session_dump_20260915.txt, brightlane_sample_payload.json

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evan Barnes <evan@brightlane.io>
Date: 2026-09-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Action needed: Brightlane POC — long-prompt stream drops & SDK behavior

Thanks for the summary, Tessa — and Evan, sorry you're seeing this. Quick notes from an initial look:

- I pulled the trace (bf3a-9c21-5532) and the runtime shows a normal token emission pattern until ~34s, then the client socket telemetry shows a FIN from the client side followed by a TCP RST. The runtime did not emit an internal 5xx.
- Hypothesis: either the SDK has an aggressive client-side idle timeout or there's an intermediate LB dropping long-lived SSE when payloads are large. Dedicated pool config does have a shorter idle keepalive in the current cluster image.

Short-term suggestions we can offer to Brightlane (pick one):
A) SDK patch: increase streaming keepalive pings and extend default client-side SSE idle to 120s (Dev, see below).
B) Service config: bump dedicated pool connection keepalive and increase per-connection buffer on their demo pool (requires infra roll).
C) Application workaround: chunking like you mentioned or shorter prompts + server-side stitching.

Dev — can you scope the SDK change (JS SDK first) and confirm if a config toggle exists that we can enable per-route? If so we can push a quick patch and cut a customer-targeted release.

I'll also log a request with infra to check LB timeouts for the dedicated demo pools.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Runtime & Routing

- The behavior is reproducible ~2/5 runs with the 12k token prompt. We saw the same pattern when trying both the hosted route and the dedicated demo route.

Subject: Re: Action needed: Brightlane POC — long-prompt stream drops & SDK behavior

Hi all,

Thanks Evan — the payload helped. Quick triage summary and proposed plan:

Findings:
- The SDK (official v0.9.4) defaults client-side SSE idle to 30s; the fork likely preserved this. When a large response yields periods >30s between SSE frames (due to token generation scheduling and model batching), the client may close the connection.
- Dedicated demo pool had a 45s LB idle, but that appears less likely given the immediate FIN from the client in traces.

Immediate mitigation (1–2 hour turnaround):
- We will cut a JS SDK 0.9.5-patch that extends SSE idle timeout to 120s and adds keepalive heartbeats every 20s. We'll publish patch notes and a one-line snippet you can add to your fork to opt-in now: 
  // snippet for Brightlane fork
  Redwood.connect({ streamingIdleMs: 120000, enableHeartbeats: true });

Medium-term (2–3 weeks):
- Add a per-route runtime flag "streaming_grace_ms" surfaced in the Console and routing API. This will let Sales Eng and Ops set a higher grace for specific demo routes without a code change. We'll prototype the API and a console toggle in the next sprint.

Regression prevention:
- Add an automated test that simulates long gaps between frames and runs against our SDK integration tests.

Action items:
- Dev: cut JS patch and attach release artifact + snippet (ETA: 2 hours).
- Karthik: confirm if we also need a runtime config change for dedicated demo pools (I'll sync with infra).
- Tessa / Logan: push patch to Brightlane fork and confirm if demos stabilize; escalate to infra if we still see drops.

I'll follow up with the patch link and a small internal playbook for support engineers to use.

- Dev Patel
Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
